chunks: From him, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, who raised it from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about a man who stole and so his hand was cut off by the establishment of proof against him, yet he did not return what he stole. What is to be done with him regarding the property of the man from whom he stole it? Is returning it not upon him? And if he claims that he has nothing with him, neither a little nor much, and that is known from him? He said: “He is made to work until he pays the last dirham that he stole.”

key_terms.آخِرَ دِرْهَمٍ: the last dirham; complete repayment without any remainder
key_terms.ادَّعَى: he claimed; asserted a defense or excuse
key_terms.بِإِقَامَةِ الْبَيِّنَةِ: by establishing the proof; through legal evidence validating the charge
key_terms.رَدُّهُ: returning it; restoring the stolen property to its owner
key_terms.سَرَقَ: stole; unlawfully took another person’s property
key_terms.فَقُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ: his hand was cut off; the prescribed hadd punishment was carried out
key_terms.يُسْتَسْعَى: he is made to work; he is compelled to earn in order to repay

ai.seo_question: If a thief’s hand is cut off, does he still have to repay the stolen property?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the legal punishment for theft does not remove the thief’s liability to restore the stolen property. If the stolen property has not been returned and the thief is known to possess nothing, he is to be made to work until he fully repays the amount taken.
